leftEvidence.title: David’s house is strengthened and then mourns

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Judah’s tents are saved first, Jerusalem is defended, David’s house is compared to God’s messenger, a spirit of grace and supplication is poured out, and families mourn separately.
points.right: The portrait says the Lord took away David’s sins, exalted his power, gave a covenant and throne, then moves through Solomon’s wisdom, desire, and the kingdom’s division.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places exaltation language gives way to piercing and widespread differentiated grief inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Davidic praise is followed by a succession remembered through wisdom and fracture inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Zechariah 12:7–14 and Sirach 47:12–25 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Sirach retains pardon, covenant, and the division after David

payload.tension: Zechariah 12:7–14 foregrounds exaltation language gives way to piercing and widespread differentiated grief; Sirach 47:12–25 foregrounds Davidic praise is followed by a succession remembered through wisdom and fracture. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
